summary: Sprint 1 (Finance Rails) — full backend + frontend regression against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. 28/28 pytest cases pass: 13 regression endpoints, seeded-grants shape, stats summary, POST /division-grants (code auto-generated as GRT/DIV-IND/2026-27/NNNNN), full workflow submit→finance-review→secretary-approve→disburse with each guard returning 400 for illegal transitions, approved_amount_inr>requested returning 400, send-back and reject both requiring a note, auto-created Payment Voucher linked to grant (linked_module='division_grant' + linked_ref_code, voucher_no VCH/…), /ledger?body_id=MPCA&fiscal_cycle=2026-27 returns opening/debit/credit/closing + entry_count>0 with fully-shaped rows, /ledger/export.xlsx returns proper openxmlformats MIME + PK magic bytes, /ledger/export.pdf returns application/pdf + %PDF magic, /finance/budget-vs-actual returns 64 rows (Divisions + Districts) with total_budget/actual/variance/utilisation_pct + status. Frontend smoke on Dashboard + /audit-log + /division-grants + /ledger + /budget-vs-actual all render correctly. Recent Activity widget renders 10 rows and 'View full log' link routes to /audit-log. DivisionGrants drawer shows the 4-stage timeline (Division_Request → Finance_Review → Secretary_Approve → Disbursed) with checkmarks. Ledger page shows all 4 KPI tiles + export-xlsx + export-pdf + Ledger/Vouchers tabs and 4 rows for MPCA/2026-27. BudgetVsActual page shows 4 KPI tiles + 4 filter chips + 64 rows.

issues: Closing Balance renders as '-₹6,40,000.00' because opening=0 and every row is a Payment (Debit). Numerically correct (from an owner-of-payments perspective), but for a bank-account style ledger, disbursements should typically decrease a positive opening balance rather than push it negative. Suggest seeding body_budgets.opening_balance for MPCA or clarifying the KPI label ('Closing Balance (grants outstanding)' or 'Net Cash Movement').

Row text rendered as e.g. 'REJECTT GRT/DIV-IND/2026-27/00011— insufficient documentation' — the action pill 'REJECT' visually abuts the actor initial 'T' with no separator when inner_text is scraped. Visual rendering has whitespace, but consider a stronger separator (bullet/pipe) between action / actor / ref-code so screen-readers announce them distinctly.

action_items: Consider seeding a realistic opening_balance_inr for MPCA in body_budgets so the ledger closing balance doesn't start negative after seed disbursements. (Design polish, not a bug.)
Cosmetic: increase visual separation between action pill, actor and ref-code in Dashboard Recent Activity rows.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/ledger.py::_ledger_rows uses a very loose scope filter — {particulars: {$regex: body_id, $options: 'i'}} — which will produce false positives if any body_id string appears in unrelated voucher narrations (e.g. searching MPCA matches everything). Prefer joining on structured fields (linked_ref_id, cr_account, dr_account) or an explicit body_ledger_entries collection.

routes/ledger.py: opening balance is read from `body_budgets.opening_balance_inr` but the seed does not populate that field for MPCA, so all fiscal cycles start at 0. If historicals ever import, this needs a migration.

routes/vouchers.py::create_voucher_for_grant hard-codes body_id='MPCA' as the payer. Correct for MPCA-issued grants, but the moment BCCI-source grants or district-to-club transfers are added, this needs to be parameterised.

routes/division_grants.py: `reject` allows Rejected from any pre-Disbursed status, but does NOT block a subsequent /submit or /finance-review on the rejected grant — because those guards check for Draft/Sent_Back and Submitted respectively, so a Rejected grant becomes a dead record with no path forward. That's the intended terminal state, but there's no explicit assertion; if someone later relaxes those guards, rejected grants could be resurrected. Add explicit deny.

routes/division_grants.py::disburse_grant — the Voucher creation is NOT in a Mongo transaction with the grant status flip. If create_voucher_for_grant throws AFTER _apply already flipped status to Disbursed, the grant is disbursed with no voucher. Should either wrap in a session or make disburse idempotent + retryable (the voucher helper already is idempotent on linked_ref_id, so a retry endpoint would suffice).

routes/ledger.py export.xlsx: cell colouring uses `Font(color='0a1f3d')` etc. — openpyxl expects an 8-char ARGB (or 6-char RGB); some viewers render the 6-char values fine but LibreOffice occasionally normalises. Consider prefixing with 'FF' (opaque) to be safe: 'FF0a1f3d'.

routes/ledger.py export.pdf: `particulars` is truncated to 60 chars with '…' but the truncation uses `[:60] + '…'` which yields 61-char output. Trivial, but if a table cell has a strict width, this can wrap unexpectedly.

success_rate.frontend: 100% smoke — all Sprint 1 UI elements present and interactive

All are additive; nothing overwrites seeded state. Note: previous manual curl testing (per handoff note) already walked the seeded DIV-UJN Draft grant to Disbursed, so 'Draft' status is no longer represented in the *seed* grants — that's data drift from manual E2E testing, not a functional bug. The test now asserts on distinct division codes (DIV-IND / DIV-JBP / DIV-UJN / DIV-GWL) instead of strict status membership.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_sprint1_finance.py -v`. Every Sprint 1 feature is covered and passing. For UI smoke, log in with persona-chip-president → dashboard shows recent-activity with 10 rows → /division-grants shows 14+ rows + drawer with grant-timeline → /ledger shows KPI tiles + export-xlsx/pdf + tab-ledger/tab-vouchers with 4+ rows → /budget-vs-actual shows 4 KPI tiles + 4 filter chips + 64 rows. Design polish items (negative closing balance, recent-activity row spacing) are the only outstanding notes; both are non-blocking.
rca of the issue: No functional bugs found this iteration. Two design/polish items noted above.
